blocks.title: Thermoregulation
blocks.text: Thermoregulation is the homeostatic process by which organisms keep their internal body temperature within a tolerable range whatever the outside temperature.

It matters because enzymes work best at an optimum temperature: below it, enzyme-substrate collisions and metabolic rate fall; well above it, enzymes denature and lose their function permanently. Cell membranes are also sensitive: heat can destroy their selective permeability and cold can make them rigid and brittle.
